meta.title: Medusa Cloud — Accounting traceability for your business
meta.description: Medusa Cloud: multi-tenant accounting trust ledger for business units. Open source Core lives at medusa-ledger.

hero.title: Ledger (Blockchain) for accounting traceability for your business
hero.lead: Hosted multi-tenant product. The open source engine is Medusa Ledger Core.

what.title: The problem it solves
what.lead: This is not “having blockchain”. It answers with evidence:
what.q: Who generated which money, who received it, how much each participant was owed, and who can prove it?
what.c1_text: The ERP says what it recorded. Medusa says what actually happened: who generated it, who approved it, how it was split and reconciled.
what.c2_text: Each business unit has different partners: an isolated chain and its own Medusa hub — no mixed money across units.
what.c3_text: Your payment gateway collects. Medusa anchors the proof (hash + block). Odoo, SAP, BI and AI can consume that truth later.
what.c4_text: A traceability, reconciliation and governance layer: who generated which money, who received it, what each party was owed, and who can prove it — in real time.

flow.title: Accounting unit flow
flow.lead: User | customer → operator → your business unit → your tenant or ERP → payments, billing and distribution → regulatory entity.

mvp.title: MVP | demo
mvp.lead: Isolated chain per unit, anchored to real payments.
mvp.i3: Live hub: blocks, pending, seal, verify chain
mvp.i4: Medusa login + access from the unit dashboard

pitch.p1: Your company has a verifiable enterprise source of truth, independent from the ERP.
pitch.p2: Trust Ledger as a Service — Blockchain-as-a-Business-Ledger per business unit.
pitch.p3: The ERP stops being the origin of truth and becomes a consumer of truth.

model.title: Open Source Core + Medusa Cloud
model.c1_text: Odoo, SAP or your ERP keep running the business.
model.c2_text: Verifiable immutable evidence layer per unit.
model.c3_text: Consumes the chain to explain and audit.
model.c4_text: Reports on demonstrable facts, not just DB rows.
model.arch_text: Medusa Core (OSS) = ledger + API. Medusa Cloud = multi-tenant, white-label, payment anchors, hubs, SLA, ERP.
model.sponsors_text: Sponsors is not only donation: it’s an international discovery channel for Core. Cloud / Business / Enterprise remain the business.

p2l.title: P2L integration
p2l.lead: Medusa Cloud is not a pilot: it runs in production inside multi-tenant P2L, with real partners and real payments.
p2l.c1_text: P2L installs @medusa-ledger/core as the ledger engine. Your ERP does not rewrite accounting — it consumes verifiable evidence per unit.
p2l.c2_text: Tuk Tuk is an active white-label tenant. Every confirmed ePayco charge creates a PAYMENT_CAPTURED anchor on that unit’s chain.
p2l.c3_text: Each brand or business unit gets an isolated ledger, its own Medusa hub and separate partners. No mixed money across brands.

pricing.title: Core, Sponsors and Cloud plans
pricing.lead: Core is open for adoption; Cloud, Business and Enterprise are the commercial path.
pricing.community_desc: Medusa Core OSS — append-only ledger + API
pricing.cloud_desc: Hosted ledger · 1 business unit · hub + anchors
pricing.enterprise_desc: SLA · compliance · ERP connectors · dedicated support

install.title: Install anywhere
install.text: Node, Spring Boot, Docker and other stacks are documented on the Open Source landing — for your technical team and architects.

erp.title: Natural evolution toward ERP
erp.lead: We don’t replace Odoo, SAP, or your ERP overnight — that’s impossible… We replace dependence on the ERP as the single source of truth.
erp.pain: We know the headache of DIAN electronic invoicing reports and public oversight and control entities. That’s why we built an accounting traceability ledger for ecosystems and businesses that need to monitor the trail of every transaction.
erp.restore_title: Medusa blockchain does not replace your ERP
erp.restore: It restores the ERP’s foundational nature and lifts the weight of accounting and fiscal responsibility off your database.
erp.g3_text: Business events → immutable ledger → ERP, AI and BI consume verifiable evidence.
erp.events_text: ORDER_CREATED, PAYMENT_AUTHORIZED, SERVICE_COMPLETED, COMMISSION_CALCULATED, SETTLEMENT_DONE, INVOICE_PAID… a fully reconstructable history.

how.title: How it works
how.lead: Three steps for partners and operators of the unit.
how.step1_text: A payment, wallet top-up or unit credit creates the business fact.
how.step2_text: The tx enters pending, then seals into a block with previousHash and SHA-256.
how.step3_text: The hub shows the chain, filters by source and verifies integrity if a hash is tampered.

cta.title: Try Medusa on the Tuk Tuk demo unit
cta.text: Tuk Tuk is the demo business unit where the ledger already runs. Open the hub, verify the chain and watch accounting traceability live.

footer.blurb: Medusa Cloud — multi-tenant accounting traceability for business units. OSS Core at medusa-ledger.

g.title: How Medusa works, piece by piece
g.lead: No tech jargon: six pieces, each with its own color. Tap one to see only what it does.
g.map_hint: Tap one to highlight it. Tap again to see everything.
g.s1_p: Each business (project) has its own ledger. The screen is the same for everyone: what changes is the project sheet that gets opened.
g.b1: Shows the months, the movements and which receipt is missing.
g.b2: Contracts, fixed costs, partners and which receipts each month needs.
g.b6: Accepts uploads of several MB without rejecting them.
g.b3: Reads the emails, keeps the keys and decides which project each file belongs to.
g.b4: Stores each receipt with its fingerprint, split by project.
g.b5: Takes the payment emails from Gmail and delivers them every hour.
g.rule: Golden rule: the project sheet travels inside the web page, so it never holds keys. Keys live only on the server.
g.s2_sub: One project = one sheet. Adding another business means adding another sheet, not writing code.
g.s2_1: Start month (genesis): the ledger's first month. No contract can start earlier.
g.s2_2: Horizon: the last month the ledger shows.
g.s2_3: Account and contracts: where the money lands and who pays what: fixed or variable fee, setup, extra modules.
g.s2_4: Fixed costs: what gets paid every month, for example hosting.
g.s2_5: Partners (nodes): who takes part; the share is split equally.
g.s2_6: Receipt rules: which support each month needs and from when.
g.s2_7: Access: the Google emails allowed to open that ledger.
g.s3_t: The screen: one month = one block
g.s3_sub: Each month closes as a block and stores the previous month's fingerprint: if someone alters a month, all the following ones break.
g.s3_p: Interactive example: tick the receipts that already arrived and watch the block status change.
g.st_ok: Month supported: every receipt, each with its fingerprint.
g.m_note: What blocks and what only warns is set in each project's sheet. Values are illustrative.
g.s3_strip: Under “Account status” a strip shows ✓ Dropbox and ✓ Script when everything is connected, or ✗ with what is missing.
g.s4_sub: Nobody downloads or uploads files: the email robot and the project folder work together, joined by one key.
g.vl_sub: One per project: one business's support never mixes with another's.
g.vl_1: Each project has its own receipts folder.
g.vl_2: Each file is stored with its SHA-256 fingerprint, a code computed from its content.
g.vl_3: If someone changes the file, the fingerprint no longer matches and it shows.
g.vx_1: The project key joins the robot and the ledger
g.vx_2: Same value on both sides. Whatever arrives with that key only enters that project; if it does not match, nothing gets in.
g.vr_sub: It lives in the Gmail inbox that receives the project's payments.
g.vr_1: Every hour it looks for just three emails: the receipt, the PSE payment and the e-invoice.
g.vr_2: It saves each email as a PDF along with its attachments (the invoice as PDF and XML).
g.vr_3: It delivers them to the server with the project key.
g.vr_4: It labels what was sent so it never repeats; anything that fails is retried the next hour.
g.flow_t: From email to ledger, in five steps
g.f1: Project Gmail: the receipt, the payment and the invoice arrive.
g.f2: Email robot: every hour it takes them and sends them.
g.f3: Server: checks the key and reads amount, receipt number and month.
g.f4: Project folder: stores the file with its fingerprint.
g.f5: Screen: the month shows the receipt ✓ or what is missing.
g.s4_manual: The only manual step is the contract deposit: it is uploaded from the ledger when you record the collection.
g.s4_safe: The robot only reads those three searches, not the rest of the inbox. Its key can deliver receipts, not read the ledger.
g.s5_1: Keeps the keys of the folder and the robot, one per project. They never travel in the web page.
g.s5_2: Reads the emails (receipt number, amount, month). If a supplier changes a text, it is fixed here without touching the robot.
g.s5_3: Keeps projects apart: each with its own folder, receipt inbox and partner room.
g.s5_4: The gate is set to let through uploads of several MB (PDFs with attachments).
g.s6_sub: One ledger, three readings. Pick your profile.
g.eco_t: Trust that does not cost an audit
g.eco_1: Less information asymmetry: every partner sees the same ledger, month by month, with the support for each movement.
g.eco_2: Lower monitoring cost: reviewing stops being a manual audit; the ledger says which month is supported.
g.eco_3: Verifiable split: each partner's share is written in the sheet and applied the same way every month.
g.eco_4: Variable income with evidence: a variable fee closes with the deposit and the amount actually collected.
g.eco_5: One business unit = one ledger: its numbers never mix with another's.
g.acc_t: Every month, with its supporting documents
g.acc_1: Support per movement: receipt, PSE payment, e-invoice (PDF and XML) and deposit stay attached to the month.
g.acc_2: Fingerprint per file: if someone changes a document, the fingerprint stops matching.
g.acc_3: The document lands in the right month: a receipt arriving on the 22nd that bills next month goes to that month; if it lands wrong, you move it.
g.acc_4: Blocks or warns: the payment blocks; the invoice that arrives days later only warns.
g.acc_5: It does not replace your accounting: your accounting software and tax reports stay the same. Medusa is a verifiable folder of supporting documents.
g.ops_t: Four pieces per project, set up once
g.ops_1: The project sheet: filled in once, with no keys.
g.ops_2: The server: receives the folder and robot keys.
g.ops_3: The Dropbox folder: one app per project, connected once.
g.ops_4: The email robot: pasted into the project Gmail with the same key as the server.
g.ops_5: The screen: the ✓ / ✗ strip confirms everything is connected.
g.gd1: One month of the ledger. It closes with its movements and receipts.
g.gd3: A code computed from a file's content. If the file changes, the code changes.
g.gd4: Each block stores the previous one's fingerprint: altering a month breaks the following ones.
g.gd5: A partner who takes part in the ledger.
g.gd6: The file that defines a project. No keys.
g.gd7: The record of a real payment inside the chain.
g.gd8: The value shared by the email robot and the server.
g.cta_t: Open it in the white label
